findings.description: HOOK_COMMANDS[tool as keyof typeof HOOK_COMMANDS]("git-safety") casts through a type the compiler cannot enforce. HOOK_COMMANDS satisfies Partial<Record<Tool, ...>>, so its inferred type has only the four keys listed, narrower than Tool. Today every tool reaching this line is guaranteed to have an entry because PROBES (guarded by `if (!probe) continue`) happens to list the same four keys by hand — an invariant two developers must remember to keep in sync across src/cli.ts and src/plan.utils.ts, not one the type system enforces. If a future tool is added to PROBES without a matching HOOK_COMMANDS entry, the lookup returns undefined and `spawnSync("sh", ["-c", undefined])` throws an unhandled TypeError, crashing doctor instead of producing a graceful FAIL like every other misconfiguration it anticipates. Not reachable with today's four wired tools, so a nit rather than a live defect — but consider deriving PROBES's key domain from HOOK_COMMANDS (e.g. `type ProbedTool = keyof typeof HOOK_COMMANDS`) so the two tables can't drift apart silently.

doctor's probe now runs each host's exact wired command instead of the adapter by path, so its fidelity for Codex and Cursor rests on wiring assumptions (their real cwd at hook-invocation time) that the matrix already flags as unverified ("Codex, opencode and Cursor wiring is derived from their documentation and has not been observed working", lines 109-111). Pre-existing and already disclosed, not introduced by this PR, but worth keeping visible now that doctor exercises those assumptions more directly.
